translation_en:
…accord with the methods of Sima Qian and Ban Gu alone; indeed, it conforms to the Way of Confucius. What further need is there to speak of Ouyang Xiu and Song Qi? Moreover, today eminent ministers and great scholars, accomplished historians and upright writers fill the literary offices, surpassing those of the Han and Tang. If the History of the Song were indeed taken up and revised, then, with a sweep of the brush, its rank growth and blemishes would be cleared away and literary elegance would emerge; its meaning would be comprehensive and its chapters concise. The history of a dynasty could thus be renewed and made ready for imperial perusal.
Nevertheless, I have something further to say. Worthy as Ouyang Xiu and Song Qi were, and carefully considered as their establishment of conventions and refinement of language may be called, they excised edicts and commands, leaving the sovereign’s words of an entire dynasty without documentary attestation. They favored unusual characters, making it easy for later readers to grow weary. Thus Liu Yuancheng held that increasing the number of events while reducing the wording was precisely the defect of the New History of the Tang; and when Sima Guang, Duke of Wen, compiled the Comprehensive Mirror, it was particularly the Old History of the Tang that he drew upon. Alas! If even these two gentlemen were thus, can we afford not to be cautious?
I therefore believe that today, when the sovereign entrusts men with this work, what matters is to put four measures into practice; and when those below undertake their duties, what matters is to consult the five aims and supplement them with the three categories. What are the four measures? First, give weight to their commission: do not let other duties distract their minds. Second, allow them ample time: do not make them careless and cursory by demanding speedy completion. Third, let them devote themselves exclusively to their work: even if selected for promotion, do not allow them immediately to leave. Fourth, seek out surviving writings: wherever works exist, leave none uncollected. If these measures are applied in overseeing the historians’ work, their commitment will be firm, and those above will have fully discharged their responsibility. What are the five aims? First, to convey the Way and moral principles; second, to make clear models and admonitions; third, …

title: 嘉靖二十二年應天府鄉試錄
text:
通古今曰著功勳曰表賢能此荀悅之論
也而干寶釋之以為若體國經野之言也
用兵征伐之權也忠孝貞烈之節也文告
專對之詞也才力伎藝之殊異也則書之
何謂三科曰敘沿革曰明罪惡曰旌怪異
此劉知幾之論也而知幾釋之以為若禮
儀用捨節文升降也君臣邪僻國家喪亂
也幽明感應禍福萌兆也則書之執是以
例宋史則筆削嚴而在下之道盡矣上下
===
各盡其道而宋史之成有不盡善者愚未
之信也管見如此幸進而教之
第五問
錢用商
同考試官教諭王批安攘之道足兵足
食二端而已此策陳說利害鑿鑿可行子其識
時務者歟宜冠本房
考試官右中允閔批談時務如燭照數計且文
詞雅健佳士也

同考試官教諭王　批〔安攘之道足兵足〕
錢用商

考試官右中允閔　批〔談時務如燭照數計且文〕

punctuated:
通古今，曰著功勳，曰表賢能。此荀悅之論也，而干寶釋之，以為若體國經野之言也，用兵征伐之權也，忠孝貞烈之節也，文告專對之詞也，才力伎藝之殊異也，則書之。何謂三科？曰敘沿革，曰明罪惡，曰旌怪異。此劉知幾之論也，而知幾釋之，以為若禮儀用捨、節文升降也，君臣邪僻、國家喪亂也，幽明感應、禍福萌兆也，則書之。執是以例宋史，則筆削嚴，而在下之道盡矣。上下各盡其道，而宋史之成有不盡善者，愚未之信也。管見如此，幸進而教之。
第五問
錢用商
同考試官教諭王批：安攘之道，足兵足食二端而已。此策陳說利害，鑿鑿可行。子其識時務者歟？宜冠本房。
考試官右中允閔批：談時務如燭照數計，且文詞雅健，佳士也。
translation_en:
…to connect past and present; to record meritorious achievements; and to bring the worthy and capable to light. These are Xun Yue’s principles. Gan Bao explained them as follows: statements concerning the organization of the capital and the ordering of the countryside; expedient strategies for deploying troops and conducting campaigns; acts of loyalty, filial devotion, steadfastness, and heroic integrity; the language of proclamations and independent responses on diplomatic missions; and exceptional abilities, skills, and arts—all these should be recorded.
What are the three categories? To recount continuity and change; to expose crimes and wrongdoing; and to mark extraordinary occurrences. These are Liu Zhiji’s principles. Zhiji explained them as follows: the adoption or abandonment of rites and ceremonies, and the elaboration or reduction of their formal details; the depravity of rulers and ministers, and disorder and ruin in the state; and interactions between the unseen and visible worlds, and emerging portents of calamity or good fortune—all these should be recorded. Apply these as standards for the History of the Song, and the decisions about what to include and omit will be rigorous, while those serving below will have fully discharged their duty. If those above and below each fully discharge their duty, I cannot believe that the completed History of the Song would fall short of excellence. Such are my limited views; I respectfully submit them and ask for your instruction.
Fifth Question
Qian Yongshang
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The way to secure peace within and repel threats from without consists of just two things: sufficient troops and sufficient provisions. This policy essay sets out the benefits and harms with precision, and its proposals are practicable. Are you not one who understands the affairs of the time? This should rank first in this examination room.
Comment by Examiner Min, Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent: He discusses current affairs as clearly as if illuminating them with a candle and as precisely as if counting and calculating. Moreover, his language is elegant and vigorous. He is an excellent scholar.

title: 嘉靖二十二年應天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官侍讀華批安攘一策正以觀諸士之
才識子能敷對詳明如此豈可以經生目之耶
欲嚴天下之大防當先天下之大計夫夷
狄不可以亂華天下之大防也兵食足而
後可以制變天下之大計也善爲國者惟
求其利而興之察其害而去之操必欲成
之心以振大有爲之勇則羣策舉邊備修
而措斯世於久安長治矣尚何有疆圉弗
靖之患哉執事發策以兵食爲問固以先
===
憂之志望承學也雖非其人敢不掇拾以
對夫胡虜桀黠密邇邊鄙窺我虛實去來
靡常其天性也故往歲嘗犯大同矣已而
寇忻代矣已而又長驅三晉矣使方其入
也堅壁清野以困之及其歸也秣馬厲兵
以擊之則殲其醜類折其驕氣彼且畏而
遁矣柰之何弗能也而使其得志以去是
雖主帥之庸瑣無策偏裨之怯懦不前而
兵食耗匱未嘗豫爲之所亦當有分其責

欲嚴天下之大防當先天下之大計夫夷
狄不可以亂華天下之大防也兵食足而
後可以制變天下之大計也善爲國者惟
求其利而興之察其害而去之操必欲成
之心以振大有爲之勇則羣策畢舉邊備修
而措斯世於久安長治矣尚何有疆圉弗
靖之患哉執事發策以兵食爲問固以先
===

punctuated:
考試官侍讀華批：安攘一策，正以觀諸士之才識。子能敷對詳明如此，豈可以經生目之耶？

欲嚴天下之大防，當先天下之大計。夫夷狄不可以亂華，天下之大防也；兵食足而後可以制變，天下之大計也。善爲國者，惟求其利而興之，察其害而去之，操必欲成之心，以振大有爲之勇，則羣策舉，邊備修，而措斯世於久安長治矣。尚何有疆圉弗靖之患哉？執事發策，以兵食爲問，固以先憂之志望承學也。雖非其人，敢不掇拾以對？夫胡虜桀黠，密邇邊鄙，窺我虛實，去來靡常，其天性也。故往歲嘗犯大同矣，已而寇忻代矣，已而又長驅三晉矣。使方其入也，堅壁清野以困之；及其歸也，秣馬厲兵以擊之，則殲其醜類，折其驕氣，彼且畏而遁矣。柰之何弗能也，而使其得志以去？是雖主帥之庸瑣無策，偏裨之怯懦不前，而兵食耗匱，未嘗豫爲之所，亦當有分其責
translation_en:
Examiner Hua, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: “This policy question on securing internal peace and repelling external threats is intended precisely to reveal the candidates’ abilities and discernment. Since you can respond with such fullness and clarity, how could you be regarded merely as a student of the Classics?”

To uphold the realm’s great defensive boundary, one must give priority to its fundamental strategic concern. That the barbarians must not be allowed to throw the Chinese realm into disorder is the great defensive boundary of the realm; that only sufficient troops and provisions make it possible to master unforeseen events is its fundamental strategic concern. Those skilled in governing a state seek out what benefits it and promote it, discern what harms it and eliminate it. Holding firmly to the determination to succeed, they summon the courage to accomplish great things. Then all useful plans will be put into effect, frontier defenses will be strengthened, and the world will be brought to enduring peace and lasting good government. What cause would remain to fear unrest along the borders? In issuing a policy question about troops and provisions, you gentlemen surely expect us students to aspire to be the first to concern ourselves with the realm’s troubles. Though I am unequal to this expectation, how could I fail to gather what insights I can and offer a response?

The northern barbarians are fierce and cunning. Living close to our frontier districts, they watch for our weaknesses and strengths, coming and going unpredictably: such is their innate disposition. Thus, in past years they invaded Datong; then they raided Xinzhou and Daizhou; then again they drove deep into the Three Jin region. Had we, when they entered, strengthened our fortifications and cleared the countryside of supplies to wear them down, and, when they withdrew, fed our horses and sharpened our weapons to strike them, we would have annihilated their vile bands and broken their arrogant spirit. They would then have fled in fear. Why were we unable to do so, allowing them instead to depart with their aims achieved? Although this resulted from the commanding generals’ mediocrity and lack of plans, and the subordinate commanders’ cowardice and failure to advance, our troops and provisions were also depleted, and no arrangements had been made beforehand to address this. There must also be those who share responsibility…

title: 嘉靖二十二年應天府鄉試錄
text:
者乎我
皇上居中制外宵旰不遑屢
詔求言欲圖後備意誠勤矣然則司兵食者
將泄泄如往時乎亦亟爲之圖以副
皇上之意乎誠圖之則所以足兵足食者不可
以不講矣故以足兵之道言之西北之地
風氣剛勁多强悍好武之人而議者欲下
招募之令非無見也但尺籍之缺動踰十
萬補葺之效責成旦夕竊恐勇者未必得
===
也而游手之徒已魚貫而附矣紀律不閑
而衣糧虚費前此京師之募士不可鑒乎
未若團結之制其效易得舉而行之可也
故必合鄉邑之丁壯什伍相結上下相聯
乘力田之暇立長以教之而給以利器復
其他徭時校其藝之上下而獎賚焉則人
皆知上德之保我非苦我以兵也樂於講
武而軍政成於鄉人人皆兵招募可弗用
矣然此特救敝之一利耳而其害兵者猶

其他徭時校其藝之上下而奬賚焉則人
皆知上德之保我非苦我以兵也樂於講
武而軍政成於鄉人人皆兵招募可弗用
矣然此特救敝之一利耳而其害兵者猶
punctuated:
者乎？我皇上居中制外，宵旰不遑，屢詔求言，欲圖後備，意誠勤矣。然則司兵食者，將泄泄如往時乎？亦亟爲之圖，以副皇上之意乎？誠圖之，則所以足兵足食者，不可以不講矣。
故以足兵之道言之，西北之地，風氣剛勁，多强悍好武之人，而議者欲下招募之令，非無見也。但尺籍之缺，動踰十萬，補葺之效，責成旦夕，竊恐勇者未必得也，而游手之徒已魚貫而附矣。紀律不閑，而衣糧虚費，前此京師之募士，不可鑒乎？未若團結之制，其效易得，舉而行之可也。
故必合鄉邑之丁壯，什伍相結，上下相聯，乘力田之暇，立長以教之，而給以利器，復其他徭，時校其藝之上下而獎賚焉。則人皆知上德之保我，非苦我以兵也，樂於講武，而軍政成於鄉，人人皆兵，招募可弗用矣。然此特救敝之一利耳，而其害兵者猶
translation_en:
…should also share the responsibility? Our Emperor directs affairs beyond the court from its center, occupied from before dawn until late at night, with no respite. He has repeatedly issued edicts soliciting advice, seeking to make preparations for the future. His concern is truly earnest. Will those responsible for troops and provisions, then, remain as idle as before? Or will they urgently devise plans to fulfill the Emperor’s intentions? If they truly undertake such planning, they must examine how to ensure sufficient troops and provisions.
To speak first of securing sufficient troops: the temper of the northwest is hardy and vigorous, and many of its people are strong, fierce, and fond of martial pursuits. Those who propose issuing an order for recruitment are therefore not without insight. Yet vacancies in the military registers readily exceed a hundred thousand, while results in filling them are demanded overnight. I fear that brave men may not necessarily be obtained, while idlers will already have joined in an unbroken stream. Untrained in military discipline, they will merely waste clothing and grain. Can the earlier recruitment of soldiers in the capital not serve as a warning? A system of organizing local men into militia units would yield results more readily; it should be put into practice.
The able-bodied men of the villages and towns must therefore be brought together, organized into groups of ten and five, and linked through a hierarchy of command. During breaks from farm labor, leaders should be appointed to train them. They should be supplied with effective weapons and exempted from other labor services. Their skills should periodically be assessed and graded, and rewards bestowed accordingly. Then everyone will understand that the benevolence of those above protects them, rather than burdening them with military service. They will gladly practice martial skills, and military organization will be established in the villages. With every man a soldier, recruitment can be dispensed with. Yet this is only one beneficial measure for remedying existing abuses; what harms the military still…

title: 嘉靖二十二年應天府鄉試錄
text:
未去也我
國初之制收天下精兵以分置邊鎭聲勢聯
屬可謂盛矣而
列聖相承注意拊循誠宜其兵之日加多也而
今顧有不然者何歟蓋必有所爲害之者
矣苟究其害之之原而刬除之則逋竄者
不可不嚴清勾之法也私役者不可不申
鬻放之律也流離者不可不施還定之恩
也庶尺伍之舊其可復乎而又習民於團
===
結焉則本末兼舉而猛士霧集銳氣雲蒸
何憂乎兵之不足哉以是兵而禦敵將焚
庭擣穴有膚功之來獻矣若夫客兵之設
雖爲諸路之援而緩急之際暫徵以張掎
角之勢則可耳若以之爲常吾恐師老財
費寧無他變耶以足食之道言之山澤之
間鹽貨繁興乃天地自然之利而議者欲
廣鬻鹽之法誠有見也然常股之制行之
已久餘鹽之課括之已盡但於商人稍優

矣苟究其害之之原而剗除之則逋竄者
不可不嚴清勾之法也私役者不可不申
禁故之律也流離者不可不施還定之恩
也庶尺伍之舊其可復乎而又習民於團
列聖相承注意拊循誠宜其兵之日加多也而
===
結焉則本末兼舉而猛士霧集銳氣雲蒸
何憂乎兵之不足哉以是兵而禦敵將焚
庭擣穴有膚功之來獻矣若夫客兵之設
雖爲諸路之援而緩急之際暫徵以張犄
角之勢則可耳若以之爲常吾恐師老財
費寧無他變耶以足食之道言之山澤之
間鹽貨繁興乃天地自然之利而議者欲
廣鬻鹽之法誠有見也然常股之制行之
已久餘鹽之課括之已盡但於商人稍優
punctuated:
未去也。我國初之制，收天下精兵以分置邊鎭，聲勢聯屬，可謂盛矣。而列聖相承，注意拊循，誠宜其兵之日加多也。而今顧有不然者，何歟？蓋必有所爲害之者矣。苟究其害之之原而刬除之，則逋竄者，不可不嚴清勾之法也；私役者，不可不申鬻放之律也；流離者，不可不施還定之恩也。庶尺伍之舊，其可復乎？而又習民於團結焉，則本末兼舉，而猛士霧集，銳氣雲蒸，何憂乎兵之不足哉？以是兵而禦敵，將焚庭擣穴，有膚功之來獻矣。若夫客兵之設，雖爲諸路之援，而緩急之際，暫徵以張掎角之勢則可耳。若以之爲常，吾恐師老財費，寧無他變耶？
以足食之道言之，山澤之間，鹽貨繁興，乃天地自然之利，而議者欲廣鬻鹽之法，誠有見也。然常股之制，行之已久；餘鹽之課，括之已盡。但於商人稍優
translation_en:
…have not yet been removed. Under the institutions established at the founding of our dynasty, elite troops from throughout the realm were gathered and stationed among the frontier garrisons. Their strength and strategic positions supported one another: this could indeed be called a flourishing military establishment. The successive sage emperors devoted their attention to caring for the troops, so their numbers surely ought to have increased daily. Yet now this is not the case. Why? There must be something harming them.
If we investigate the sources of this harm and eradicate them, then, for those who have fled, we must rigorously enforce the procedures for checking military registers and apprehending those liable for service; for those employed in private service, we must reaffirm the statutes against selling release from military duty; and for those displaced and scattered, we must extend the favor of return and resettlement. Might the former military ranks [?] then be restored? If we also train the people in organized local militia units, we will address both fundamentals and subsidiary measures. Stalwart soldiers will gather like mist, and martial ardor will rise like clouds. Why worry that the troops are insufficient? With such troops to resist the enemy, we shall burn their courts and strike their lairs, and great achievements will be presented to the throne.
As for troops brought in from elsewhere, although they serve as reinforcements for the various regions, it is acceptable only to summon them temporarily in emergencies to establish a mutually supporting position against the enemy. If this becomes a permanent practice, I fear that the army will grow weary and resources will be squandered. Could further disturbances fail to arise?
As for ensuring adequate provisions, salt is produced abundantly amid the mountains and marshes: it is a natural bounty of Heaven and Earth. Those who propose expanding the arrangements for selling salt certainly have some insight. Yet the system of regular salt allotments has long been in operation, and the revenues from surplus salt have already been fully tapped. If only the merchants were treated somewhat more generously…

title: 嘉靖二十二年應天府鄉試錄
text:
恤之而中納之徒即颺舉以赴矣令不必
更而利自有餘邇者淮浙之歲辦不可驗
乎顧惟屯田之政其壞已極變而通之可
也故必籍邊郡之屯地檢其隱占辨其瘠
肥授可耕之人盡力以甸之而優以番休
寬其征稅時稽其業之勤惰而勸相焉則
人皆知上德之育我非勞我以屯也勤於
務本而地利廣於邊在在皆穀鹽政亦有
資矣然此特補偏之一利耳而其害食者
猶未去也我
國初之制計諸省常賦以分餽邊士轉輸絡
繹可謂富矣而
列聖相承多方培植誠宜其食之日加豐也而
今顧有不然者何歟亦必有所以害之者
矣苟求其害之之故而釐正之則倚奸而
負者不得不責辦於撫臣也遇災而蠲者
不得不取償於司徒也張虛數而掊剋者
不得不致刑於將領也庶餽饟之舊其可

translation_en:
…show them consideration, and those who deliver grain in exchange for salt certificates will promptly hasten to participate. The regulations need not be changed, and ample benefits will follow of themselves. Do not the annual receipts of the Huai and Zhe salt regions in recent years provide proof? As for the administration of military agricultural colonies, its deterioration has reached an extreme; it should be adapted to restore its effective operation. The colony lands in the frontier commanderies must therefore be registered, concealed encroachments investigated, and barren and fertile land distinguished. The land should be allotted to people capable of cultivating it, who should devote their efforts to working the fields. They should be favored with rest in rotation and lighter taxes, and their diligence or negligence in farming should be inspected periodically, with encouragement and assistance provided. Then everyone will understand that the benevolence of their superiors nurtures them, rather than merely imposing the toil of colony farming upon them. They will diligently pursue agriculture, the fundamental occupation; the land’s yield will increase along the frontier, and grain will be available everywhere. The salt administration, too, will thereby gain support. Yet this is merely one benefit that remedies a particular deficiency; the causes that impair the grain supply will still not have been removed.
Under the institutions established at the founding of our dynasty, the regular taxes of the provinces were assessed and apportioned to provision the frontier soldiers. Supplies arrived in an uninterrupted stream, and could well be called abundant. Successive sage emperors fostered these arrangements in many ways, so the grain supply ought indeed to have grown more plentiful each day. Why, then, is this now not the case? There must also be causes impairing it. If we seek out those causes and rectify them, then, for arrears incurred through reliance on corrupt influence, we must hold the grand coordinators responsible for securing payment; for taxes remitted because of disasters, we must obtain replacement funds from the Minister of Revenue; and for inflated figures and extortion, we must impose punishment upon the military commanders. Then perhaps the former arrangements for military provisioning might…

title: 嘉靖二十二年應天府鄉試錄
text:
復乎而又致𪠘於鹽法屯田焉則源流並
濬而居有積倉行有裹糧何患乎食之不
足哉以是食而養兵將投石超乘有餘勇
之可賈矣若夫
内帑之儲雖為軍國之用而師旅之興暫發
以備賞賚之需則可耳若以之為常吾恐
外重内輕寧無後悔耶雖然是數者任之
得其人則愚之所言皆要言也不得其人
則愚之所言皆費辭也觀諸昔人之蹟益
===
信矣如晁錯議徙民於漢而塞下實常清
募驍勇於唐而武牢敗商鞅以什伍相收
而秦國强安石以保丁番上而宋民怨代
菹煑海肇於管仲而桓公用伯榷鹽官糶
昉於平叔而韓愈致譏留屯金城克國務
蓄積而取勝置務襄州耿望借耡夫而生
擾嗚呼均之為招募也團結也鹽法也屯
田也惟其人用之不同而成敗頓殊得失
懸判如此是誠在人不在法也可弗慎歟

足哉以是食而養兵將投石超乘有餘勇
之可賈矣若夫
內帑之儲雖爲軍國之用而師旅之興暫發
以備賞賚之需則可耳若以之爲常吾恐
外重內輕寧無後悔耶雖然是數者任之
得其人則愚之所言皆要言也不得其人
則愚之所言皆贅辭也觀諸昔人之蹟益
===
信矣如晁錯議徙民於漢而塞下實常清
募驍勇於唐而武牢敗商鞅以什伍相收
而秦國強安石以保丁畓上而宋民怨伐
菹萊海肇於管仲而桓公用伯權鹽官糶
昉於平叔而韓愈致譏留屯金城充國務
蓄積而取勝置務襄州耿望借耨夫而生
擾嗚呼均之爲招募也團結也鹽法也屯
田也惟其人用之不同而成敗頓殊得失
懸判如此是誠在人不在法也可弗慎歟
punctuated: 復乎？而又致𪠘於鹽法、屯田焉，則源流並濬，而居有積倉，行有裹糧，何患乎食之不足哉？以是食而養兵，將投石超乘，有餘勇之可賈矣。若夫内帑之儲，雖為軍國之用，而師旅之興，暫發以備賞賚之需則可耳。若以之為常，吾恐外重内輕，寧無後悔耶？雖然，是數者，任之得其人，則愚之所言皆要言也；不得其人，則愚之所言皆費辭也。觀諸昔人之蹟，益信矣。如晁錯議徙民於漢，而塞下實；常清募驍勇於唐，而武牢敗。商鞅以什伍相收，而秦國强；安石以保丁番上，而宋民怨。代菹煑海，肇於管仲，而桓公用伯；榷鹽官糶，昉於平叔，而韓愈致譏。留屯金城，克國務蓄積而取勝；置務襄州，耿望借耡夫而生擾。嗚呼！均之為招募也、團結也、鹽法也、屯田也，惟其人用之不同，而成敗頓殊，得失懸判如此。是誠在人不在法也，可弗慎歟？
translation_en:
…be restored? If attention is also given [?] to the salt administration and military agricultural colonies, both source and stream will be dredged clear: troops in garrison will have grain accumulated in granaries, and troops on the march will carry provisions. Why then worry that food will be insufficient? Nourished with these provisions, the soldiers will have strength enough to hurl stones and leap into chariots, with courage to spare for use in battle. As for the reserves of the palace treasury, although they serve military and state purposes, it is acceptable to release them temporarily when armies are mobilized, to meet the need for rewards. But if this becomes regular practice, I fear that the outer administration will grow strong while the inner treasury grows weak. Could there be no subsequent regret? Nevertheless, if these several measures are entrusted to the right men, everything I have humbly said is essential counsel; if the right men are not found, everything I have said is wasted words. Examining the deeds of men of former times makes this still more certain.

For example, Chao Cuo proposed relocating people under the Han, and the frontier became well populated; Changqing recruited brave warriors under the Tang, yet suffered defeat at Wulao. Shang Yang organized households into mutually responsible groups of ten and five, and Qin became strong; Anshi made militia men report for duty in rotation, and the people of Song became resentful. The practice described as “dai ju” [?] and boiling seawater for salt originated with Guan Zhong, and Duke Huan thereby attained hegemony; monopolizing salt and selling it through official agencies began with Pingshu, and drew criticism from Han Yu. Keeping troops to farm at Jincheng, Keguo [?] concentrated on accumulating supplies and achieved victory; establishing an agency at Xiangzhou, Geng Wang [?] requisitioned agricultural laborers and caused disruption. Alas! These were alike measures for recruiting troops, organizing local forces, administering salt, and establishing military agricultural colonies. Yet because the men implementing them differed, success and failure diverged sharply, and gains and losses were as far apart as this. It truly depends on the men, not on the methods. Can we fail to exercise care?

title: 嘉靖二十二年應天府鄉試錄
text:
夫得人之說似為常談而於足食足兵之
務至為要切雖聖賢復起莫之能易矣然
而
今日之所少者則非人也搢紳之士議論相
高介胄之流磨厲待用顧在上者所以駕
馭何如耳朱子嘗論禦夷有曰其具不在
兵食而在紀綱紀綱者何辨賢否以定上
下之分也核功罪以公賞罰之施也惟
九重之上振其紀綱以駕馭斯世則一舉措
===
而内外惕息以從焉一號令而大小踴躍
以趨焉智者盡其謀勇者竭其力懦者鼓
其氣偽者獻其誠事無不集而功無不成
中國常尊而四夷來王矣區區小醜又何足
言哉一得之愚如此執事倘采而用之未
必無補於安攘之道也

九重之上振其紀綱以駕馭斯世則一舉措
===
而內外惕息以從焉一號令而大小踴躍
以趨焉智者盡其謀勇者竭其力懦者鼓
其氣僞者獻其誠事無不集而功無不成
中國常尊而四夷來王矣區區小醜又何足
言哉一得之愚如此執事倘采而用之未
必無補於安攘之道也
punctuated: 夫得人之說，似為常談，而於足食足兵之務，至為要切。雖聖賢復起，莫之能易矣。然而今日之所少者，則非人也。搢紳之士，議論相高；介胄之流，磨厲待用。顧在上者所以駕馭何如耳。朱子嘗論禦夷，有曰：「其具不在兵食，而在紀綱。」紀綱者何？辨賢否以定上下之分也，核功罪以公賞罰之施也。惟九重之上，振其紀綱以駕馭斯世，則一舉措而内外惕息以從焉，一號令而大小踴躍以趨焉。智者盡其謀，勇者竭其力，懦者鼓其氣，偽者獻其誠。事無不集，而功無不成，中國常尊，而四夷來王矣。區區小醜，又何足言哉！一得之愚如此，執事倘采而用之，未必無補於安攘之道也。
translation_en: The argument that one must obtain the right men may seem commonplace, yet it is of the utmost importance in securing sufficient provisions and troops. Even if the sages and worthies were to rise again, they could not alter it. Yet what we lack today is not men. Men of the official class vie with one another in lofty discussion, while those who wear armor and helmets hone their skills and await employment. Everything depends upon how those above direct them. Master Zhu once said, in discussing defense against the barbarians: “The means lie not in troops and provisions, but in order and discipline.” What is meant by order and discipline? Distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy to establish their respective places above and below, and examining achievements and offenses to ensure fairness in dispensing rewards and punishments. If only His Majesty, within the ninefold palace, would invigorate this order and discipline to direct the realm, then with each action, those at court and beyond would comply in trembling awe; with each command, high and low alike would hasten eagerly to obey. The wise would contribute all their counsel, the brave exert all their strength, the timid summon their courage, and the insincere offer their sincerity. Every undertaking would succeed and every achievement be brought to completion. The Central Kingdom would remain forever honored, and the barbarians of the four quarters would come to acknowledge its sovereign. What need would there then be even to speak of those petty miscreants? Such is this fool’s single insight. If you, honored examiners, should adopt and employ it, it might well contribute to the way of securing peace within and repelling threats from without.

皇上御極以來恢弘
祖業夙夜兢兢惟賢俊是任治功大
彰然賢俊之任其初進也羅以
科目而始於鄉鄉之貢之也第
其文而舉錯之量其地之産而
多寡焉此我

punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄後序

皇上御極以來，恢弘祖業，夙夜兢兢，惟賢俊是任，治功大彰。然賢俊之任，其初進也，羅以科目，而始於鄉。鄉之貢之也，第其文而舉錯之，量其地之産而多寡焉。此我國家制也。

是歲秋，臣察、臣如霖恭承簡命，來主應天試事。士之操觚挾牘而進者，四千五百有竒。三試之，閱其文，可取者殆數浮於制乎！而制不敢踰也。嗚呼！
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Provincial Examination

Since His Majesty ascended the throne, he has extended and glorified his ancestors’ achievements. Vigilant morning and night, he has entrusted responsibilities solely to worthy and talented men, and the accomplishments of his government have become abundantly manifest. Yet when such men first enter service, they are gathered through the examination system, beginning with the Provincial Examination. In presenting its candidates, each province ranks their compositions and selects or sets them aside accordingly; the number selected varies according to the talent the region produces. This is our dynasty’s established system.

In the autumn of this year, we, your servants Cha and Rulin, respectfully received appointment by imperial selection and came to preside over the examination at Yingtian. More than four thousand five hundred scholars came forward bearing writing tablets and documents. We examined them in three sessions and read their compositions: the number worthy of selection surely exceeded the prescribed quota! Yet we dared not exceed that quota. Ah! …

title: 嘉靖二十二年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇上作人之效盛矣哉夫自古天眷
興隆之運而人才乃生上有躬
行之化而人才乃成成而盛者
非化乆而入人深弗能也備是
三者其惟文王乎故思齊之詩
歌詠文王之德交神人居宫廟
處險夷至詳且悉而必以古之
===
人無斁譽髦斯士終焉夫無斁
敬之謂也文王所以敷宣萬化
表儀四方者咸本於敬而又引
之以壽考其承休而興者烏可
量耶成人有德小子有造有由
然也文王旣沒道化之隆不在
今日乎

表儀四方者咸本於敬而又引
之以壽考其承休而興者烏可
量耶成人有德小子有造有由

今日乎
punctuated: 皇上作人之效盛矣哉！夫自古天眷興隆之運，而人才乃生；上有躬行之化，而人才乃成。成而盛者，非化乆而入人深弗能也。備是三者，其惟文王乎？故《思齊》之詩，歌詠文王之德，交神人，居宫廟，處險夷，至詳且悉，而必以「古之人無斁，譽髦斯士」終焉。夫無斁，敬之謂也。文王所以敷宣萬化、表儀四方者，咸本於敬，而又引之以壽考，其承休而興者，烏可量耶？「成人有德，小子有造」，有由然也。文王旣沒，道化之隆，不在今日乎？
translation_en: …How flourishing are the results of His Majesty’s cultivation of men of talent! Since antiquity, talented men have emerged when Heaven favors an age of prosperity; they have matured when the ruler transforms them through his own conduct. For such men to mature and flourish, that transforming influence must endure long and penetrate deeply into people’s hearts. Who but King Wen possessed all three conditions? Thus the ode “Si Qi” (“Thinking of the Dignified One”) praises King Wen’s virtue in his dealings with spirits and men, in his palace and ancestral temple, and amid peril and ease, in the fullest detail; yet it concludes with the words: “The man of old was unwearying, nurturing these outstanding scholars.” To be unwearying means to be reverent. King Wen’s dissemination of transforming influences and his example to the four quarters were all rooted in reverence. Moreover, he prolonged these through a long life: how could one measure the number of those who received his beneficence and rose to distinction? “The grown men possessed virtue; the young had attained accomplishment”: there was a reason for this. Now that King Wen has passed away, is it not in our own day that the Way and its transforming influence flourish?

title: 嘉靖二十二年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇上握符凝
命履中興之運修己治民惟敬惟
一而又著爲
箴訓以示天下
聖澤之所浸潤淳風之所噓拂於茲
二紀誠與文王先後一揆矣是
以徼外之夷猶知回面慕義遐
===
陬之人無不竦企而談詩書而
况於
南畿根本之地乎乃今績學之士
思躡風雲之會若是乎其多也
固宜然臣之所取特以文耳其
德與造詎亦有與文不相協者
乎臣聞之文者心之經緯也孝
alt_text:
皇上握符凝
命履中興之運修己治民惟敬惟
一而又著爲
箴訓以示天下
聖澤之所浸潤淳風之所噓拂於兹
二紀誠與文王先後一揆矣是
以徼外之夷猶知回面慕義遐
陬之人無不竦企而談詩書而
===
況於
南畿根本之地乎乃今績學之士
思躡風雲之會若是乎其多也
固宜然〔臣〕之所取特以文耳其
德與造詎亦有與文不相協者
乎〔臣〕聞之文者心之經緯也孝
punctuated: 皇上握符凝命，履中興之運，修己治民，惟敬惟一，而又著爲箴訓，以示天下。聖澤之所浸潤，淳風之所噓拂，於茲二紀，誠與文王先後一揆矣。是以徼外之夷猶知回面慕義，遐陬之人無不竦企而談詩書，而况於南畿根本之地乎？乃今績學之士，思躡風雲之會，若是乎其多也，固宜然。臣之所取，特以文耳，其德與造，詎亦有與文不相協者乎？臣聞之：文者，心之經緯也。孝
translation_en: His Majesty holds the token of sovereignty and secures the Mandate, presiding over an age of dynastic resurgence. In cultivating himself and governing the people, he maintains reverence and singleness of purpose. He has also composed admonitions and instructions to make them known throughout the realm. His sagely beneficence has permeated all, and his pure moral influence has gently stirred them, for these two twelve-year cycles. Truly, though living in different ages, he and King Wen follow the same principles. Thus even the peoples beyond the frontiers know to turn toward him and admire righteousness; those in distant corners all look up with eager respect and discuss the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents. How much more must this be so in the Southern Metropolitan Region, the foundational territory of the realm! It is therefore only fitting that so many scholars of sustained learning should now aspire to seize this auspicious opportunity for advancement. Yet your servant has selected them solely on the basis of their writing. Might there be some whose virtue and attainments do not accord with their writing? Your servant has heard: writing is the warp and weft of the heart. Those who are filial …

title: 嘉靖二十二年應天府鄉試錄
text:
悌者其詞温剛毅者其詞雄直
亮者其詞切通敏者其詞辯廉
介者其詞潔夫温而有理也雄
而不肆也切而不訐也辯而不
騁也潔而不傲也則其中之持
敬又必然矣諸士之文夫孰不
類於此乎臣於是因其文徵其
===
德與造並慶其遭時奮庸而無
遺伏之歎也雖然臣復竊有慮
焉昔者子夏孔門之高第也悅
夫子之道已深一旦出見紛華
而心動焉甚矣執德之難也諸
士行將試春闈對
大廷登於庶位有禄秩之榮使遷
alt_text:
第者其詞溫剛毅者其詞雄直
亮者其詞切通敏者其詞辯廉
介者其詞潔夫溫而有理也雄
而不肆也切而不訐也辯而不
騁也潔而不傲也則其中之持
敬又必然矣諸士之文夫孰不
類於此乎臣於是因其文徵其
===
德與造益慶其遭時奮庸而無
遺伏之歎也雖然臣復竊有慮
焉昔者子夏孔門之高第也悅
夫子之道已深一旦出見紛華
而心動焉甚矣執德之難也諸
士行將試春闈對
大廷登於庶位有禄秩之榮使遷
punctuated:
悌者其詞温，剛毅者其詞雄，直亮者其詞切，通敏者其詞辯，廉介者其詞潔。夫温而有理也，雄而不肆也，切而不訐也，辯而不騁也，潔而不傲也，則其中之持敬又必然矣。諸士之文，夫孰不類於此乎？臣於是因其文徵其德與造，並慶其遭時奮庸而無遺伏之歎也。
雖然，臣復竊有慮焉。昔者子夏，孔門之高第也，悅夫子之道已深，一旦出見紛華而心動焉。甚矣，執德之難也！諸士行將試春闈，對大廷，登於庶位，有禄秩之榮，使遷
translation_en:
…and fraternal respect express themselves with warmth; the firm and resolute, with vigor; the upright and sincere, with directness; the perceptive and quick-witted, with eloquence; and the incorruptible and principled, with purity. If their warmth is governed by principle, their vigor is free of excess, their directness avoids exposing others’ faults, their eloquence avoids extravagance, and their purity is without arrogance, then they must also maintain reverent attentiveness within. Whose writing among these scholars does not resemble this? Your servant has therefore inferred their virtue and attainments from their writing, and rejoices that they have met with an opportune age in which to exert themselves in service, leaving no cause to lament that worthy men remain overlooked and obscure.
Even so, your servant privately harbors a further concern. In former times, Zixia was an outstanding disciple of Confucius and already took profound delight in the Master’s Way. Yet one day, on going out and seeing worldly splendors, his heart was stirred. How difficult it is to hold fast to virtue! These scholars will soon sit the spring Metropolitan Examination, answer questions at the Palace Examination, ascend to the various offices, and enjoy the honors of salary and rank. If they should be swayed…

title: 嘉靖二十二年應天府鄉試錄
text:
於外物以變其初豈所望於諸
士哉其尚恒思
聖訓而以敬一相勵翼演之文者勤
而行之以昭其德造全其譽髦
而顯庸其勳業則不惟弼成太
平有道之長以副
皇上任賢俊之意而主司亦與有光
===
矣諸士勉乎哉
右春坊右中允兼翰林院修撰
閔如霖謹序
alt_text:
於外物以變其初豈所望於諸
士哉其尚恒思
聖訓而以敬一相勵翼演之文者勸
而行之以昭其德造全其譽髦
而顯庸其勳業則不惟弼成太
平有道之長以副
皇上任賢俊之意而主司亦與有光
===
矣諸士勉乎哉
右春坊右中允兼翰林院修撰
閔如霖謹序
punctuated:
於外物以變其初，豈所望於諸士哉？其尚恒思聖訓，而以敬一相勵翼，演之文者勤而行之，以昭其德造，全其譽髦，而顯庸其勳業，則不惟弼成太平有道之長，以副皇上任賢俊之意，而主司亦與有光矣。諸士勉乎哉！
右春坊右中允兼翰林院修撰閔如霖謹序。
translation_en:
…by external things, thereby changing their original resolve—could this be what we hope for from you gentlemen? May you constantly reflect upon the sagely instructions and encourage and support one another in reverent single-mindedness. Diligently put into practice what you have expounded in writing, thereby manifesting your moral attainments, preserving your reputation and excellence [?], and achieving distinction through meritorious service. Then you will not only help perpetuate an age of peace governed by the Way, fulfilling His Majesty’s intention in employing worthy and talented men; the officials presiding over the examination will also share in your glory. Strive, gentlemen!
Respectfully prefaced by Min Rulin, Right Companion of the Right Spring Office, concurrently Senior Compiler of the Hanlin Academy.
